doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: The teaching degree he never used
summary: Student teaching in Yonkers ended when he asked off for a record date.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: But you weren’t taking jazz courses, right?
Oh no, no. They couldn’t understand that.
So you got a degree in teaching?
Right. Did you ever really use it?

When I was doing my student teaching they had me go to Yonkers to do — a guy was doing jury duty, you know, the band whatever. So they said you go up there for two weeks. So I went up there and about the second or third day I went to the principal and I said, “I got a record date can I take off tomorrow?” He said, “what’s a record date?” I said oh, Jesus, not for me. So I got out of that. I never used it.
Oh that’s funny, what’s a record date.
Yeah. If he didn’t know what a record date was, I don’t belong there. I had to get out. You can’t turn record dates down. I mean then you end up a roadie.
Okay. You’re right back where you started.
Yeah. So that was that. I forgot about the teaching.
But you did get the degree.
My wife wants me to use it, I said no, you know, not now.
